ECE 685 | Power Systems Design L33
Power Flow II
Construction of the bus admittance matrix
Buxin She
Mike Wiegers Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering

Lecture outline
1 Write the bus equations, form their matrix, then construct Y-bus for a general
network.
2 Extend the matrix for shunts; transformer tap corrections are optional.
3 Calculate Y-bus and bus power injections, then update the matrix for added
equipment.
ECE 685 | Power Flow II 2/40

PART 1
Building Y-bus from the network
Write the known three-bus equations in matrix form. Interpret their
coefficients, then extend the construction to a general network.

Why use matrix form?
Branch current relations and KCL already give an equation at each bus. For example,
𝐼1 = 𝑦 12(𝑉1 − 𝑉2) + 𝑦13(𝑉1 − 𝑉3).
A large network
Each bus has different connections.
Managing a separate expression for
every bus becomes cumbersome as the
network grows.
Computer implementation
Store voltage coefficients in a matrix.
Software assembles them from branch
data, then evaluates all bus currents with
one matrix operation.
I = YbusV
I, V: vectors of bus currents and voltages. Ybus: bus admittance matrix.

Series model: unity taps, no charging or bus shunts.

Collect the voltage coefficients
Expand each equation and collect terms in the order 𝑉1, 𝑉2, 𝑉3.
For bus 1,
𝐼1 = 𝑦 12𝑉1 − 𝑦12𝑉2 + 𝑦13𝑉1 − 𝑦13𝑉3
= (𝑦 12 + 𝑦13)𝑉1 − 𝑦12𝑉2 − 𝑦13𝑉3.
Applying the same step at buses 2 and 3 gives
𝐼2 = −𝑦 12𝑉1 + (𝑦12 + 𝑦23)𝑉2 − 𝑦23𝑉3,
𝐼3 = −𝑦 13𝑉1 − 𝑦23𝑉2 + (𝑦13 + 𝑦23)𝑉3.

The off-diagonal entries stay unchanged.

Update the diagonal entries first, then the off-diagonal entries. Replace only this
branch’s coefficients and retain all other device contributions.

2 Construct diagonal and off-diagonal entries from network connections and
device data.
3 Add shunt admittances to the diagonal; apply transformer tap corrections as an
